import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1108

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1108](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1108)
-/

open Nat Filter BigOperators

namespace Erdos1108

/--
The set $A = \left\{ \sum_{n\in S}n! : S\subset \mathbb{N}\text{ finite}\right\}$ of all finite
sums of distinct factorials.
-/
def FactorialSums : Set ℕ :=
  {m : ℕ | ∃ S : Finset ℕ, m = ∑ n ∈ S, n.factorial}

/--
A number is powerful if each prime factor appears with exponent at least 2.
-/
def IsPowerful (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ n → p ^ 2 ∣ n
/--
For each $k \geq 2$, does the set $A = \left\{ \sum_{n\in S}n! : S\subset \mathbb{N}\text{ finite}\right\}$ of all finite sums of distinct factorials contain only finitely many $k$-th powers?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1108.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 2,
    Set.Finite { a | a ∈ FactorialSums ∧ ∃ m : ℕ, m ^ k = a } := by
  sorry

/--
Does the set $A = \left\{ \sum_{n\in S}n! : S\subset \mathbb{N}\text{ finite}\right\}$ of all finite sums of distinct factorials contain only finitely many powerful numbers?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1108.parts.ii :
     answer(sorry) ↔ {a ∈ FactorialSums | IsPowerful a}.Finite := by
  sorry

end Erdos1108

reformulations.difference: The Lean predicate IsPowerful includes 0, whereas the standard definition of a powerful number requires positivity. The empty factorial sum also puts 0 in FactorialSums.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive integers, IsPowerful is exactly the standard prime-divisibility definition. Restricting the set in part (ii) to positive integers removes only 0, which cannot change finiteness. The precise finiteness equivalence was proved as part_ii_positive_equiv in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. This argument concerns the value 0, not restricting the factorial indices to positive integers.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/Ob1 — bibliographic entry read via https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/Ob1; the book itself was not retrieved

B. Brindza and P. Erdős, “On some diophantine problems involving powers and factorials,” J. Austral. Math. Soc. (Series A) 51 (1991), 1–7, §1: https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/S1446788700033255
review.notes:
Checked both definitions and both theorem statements, including quantifier scope, answer placeholders, finiteness semantics, and boundary cases. The source page and current external status database both record the problem as open.

The factorial-index convention is supported by the displayed source formula and linked OEIS A051761, which explicitly treats 0! and 1! as distinct and includes 4 = 0! + 1! + 2!. A115645 uses a different convention; the source forum explicitly describes the linked sequences as variants. I have not assumed that positive-index and nonnegative-index factorial sums give equivalent finiteness questions.

Scratch checks compiled successfully, including small factorial-sum computations, IsPowerful ↔ Nat.Powerful for every natural number, unboundedness of FactorialSums, and the positivity/finiteness equivalence. Direct access to the problem page was Cloudflare-blocked; its 9 September 2026 archive was used. The reviewed file matches the specified commit byte-for-byte.
